flows.title: Run the service
flows.goal: The user can start the service with the intended configuration, have the database prepared, see where it is listening, and verify it is healthy.

milestones.claimTitle: Each configuration setting has the documented default value and is overridden by its corresponding environment variable.
milestones.note: Configuration determines the database and listening settings used when the service starts.

milestones.claimTitle: On startup, the service applies every migration in `migrations/` against the configured database before it starts listening.
milestones.note: The service prepares the configured database before accepting requests.

milestones.claimTitle: Once the service is up, it prints one line naming the address it is listening on and the database it is using, with the database password masked.
milestones.note: After startup completes, the user can see the listening address and database without exposing the password.

milestones.claimTitle: When the service is listening, `GET /healthz` responds with status `200` and body `{"status":"ok","service":"bookclub"}`.
milestones.note: The health response confirms the listening service is ready.

flows.title: Add a book and prevent duplicate ISBNs
flows.goal: A member can add a book with a normalized ISBN, and the shelf refuses another copy of the same ISBN even when written differently.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books accepts a valid ISBN-10 or ISBN-13 with or without hyphens and spaces and stores the thirteen-digit form returned in the book's isbn field.
milestones.note: The first add establishes the ISBN on the shelf.

milestones.claimTitle: Adding an ISBN that is already on the shelf is answered 409 with {"error":"that book is already on the shelf"} and leaves the shelf unchanged, including when the duplicate is only equivalent after ISBN normalisation.
milestones.note: The duplicate add acts on the ISBN already stored by the previous step.

flows.title: Finish a book and re-stamp it
flows.goal: A member can mark a book finished, and finishing it again updates the finishedAt stamp.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books/{id}/finish moves a book to finished, stamps finishedAt with the moment it was marked, and answers 200 with the book in its new state.
milestones.note: The book first moves into the finished state.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books/{id}/finish re-stamps finishedAt for a book that is already finished.
milestones.note: The second finish acts on the already-finished book from the previous step.

flows.title: Read archived books
flows.goal: Archived books are hidden from the shelf list and return the archived error when requested directly.

milestones.claimTitle: An archived book does not appear in GET /books.
milestones.note: The list view excludes the archived book.

milestones.claimTitle: GET /books/{id} for an archived book answers 410 with {"error":"book archived"}.
milestones.note: A direct read of that archived book reports that it is archived.

flows.title: Read without credentials and block unauthenticated changes
flows.goal: Anyone can read books, while attempts to change the shelf without a valid member token are rejected without writing anything.

milestones.claimTitle: GET /books and GET /books/{id} are answered without requiring credentials.
milestones.note: The user can read the shelf before authenticating.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books and POST /books/{id}/finish without a member token, or with a token the club's secret does not verify, are answered 401 with {"error":"authentication required"} and nothing is written.
milestones.note: The same unauthenticated or invalidly authenticated user cannot change the shelf.

flows.title: Reject an invalid ISBN
flows.goal: A user who submits a value that is not a valid ISBN gets the documented validation error.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books refuses a value that is neither a valid ISBN-10 nor a valid ISBN-13 with status 400 and {"error":"isbn must be a valid ISBN-10 or ISBN-13"}.
milestones.note: This is a validation failure path for adding a book.

flows.title: Keep a member token working after restart
flows.goal: A member remains able to use the same token after the service restarts.

milestones.claimTitle: A member token keeps working after the service restarts.
milestones.note: This is the persistence expectation for member authentication.

flows.title: Print configuration
flows.goal: The user can inspect the configuration the service would use with the database password masked.

milestones.claimTitle: `bookclub config` prints the configuration the service would use, one setting per line, with the database password replaced by `***`, and exits `0`.
milestones.note: This is the successful configuration inspection path.

flows.title: Reject unsupported database scheme
flows.goal: The user gets a clear error when the configured database scheme is not supported.

milestones.claimTitle: If `DATABASE_URL` names a non-Postgres scheme, `bookclub config` writes `error: unsupported database scheme "<scheme>" — bookclub speaks postgres and postgresql` to stderr and exits `2`.
milestones.note: This is the configuration error path.

flows.title: Print thirteen-digit ISBN
flows.goal: The user can provide a valid ISBN and receive its thirteen-digit form.

milestones.claimTitle: `bookclub isbn <value>` prints the thirteen-digit form of a valid ISBN-10 or ISBN-13, ignoring hyphens and spaces in the input, and exits `0`.
milestones.note: This is the successful ISBN conversion path.

flows.title: Reject invalid ISBN
flows.goal: The user gets a clear error when the provided ISBN value is invalid.

milestones.claimTitle: When `bookclub isbn <value>` receives a value that is not a valid ISBN, it writes `error: "<value>" is not a valid ISBN` to stderr and exits `2`.
milestones.note: This is the invalid ISBN error path.

flows.title: Require ISBN value
flows.goal: The user gets a clear error when asking for ISBN conversion without a value.

milestones.claimTitle: Calling `bookclub isbn` with no value writes `error: isbn needs a value` and exits `2`.
milestones.note: This is the missing ISBN value error path.

flows.title: Show help
flows.goal: The user can request usage text successfully.

milestones.claimTitle: `bookclub --help` or `bookclub -h` writes the usage to stdout and exits `0`.
milestones.note: This is the explicit help path.

flows.title: Show version
flows.goal: The user can request the CLI version successfully.

milestones.claimTitle: `bookclub --version` or `bookclub -V` writes `bookclub` followed by the version and exits `0`.
milestones.note: This is the version reporting path.

flows.title: Require a command
flows.goal: The user gets usage text as an error when running the CLI without arguments.

milestones.claimTitle: Run with no arguments, `bookclub` writes the usage text to stderr and exits `2`.
milestones.note: This is the no-arguments error path.

flows.title: Reject unknown commands
flows.goal: The user gets a clear error when entering a command that is not defined.

milestones.claimTitle: An undefined `bookclub` command writes `error: unknown command "<name>"` to stderr and exits `2`.
milestones.note: This is the unknown command error path.

flows.title: Add, list, retrieve, and finish a book
flows.goal: A member can add a book, see it on the shelf with the expected list representation, retrieve it by id, and mark it finished.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books with a valid member token and an application/json body containing isbn, title, and author responds with 201 and a JSON representation of the book that was added.
milestones.note: The path starts with a member adding a book to the shelf.

milestones.claimTitle: GET /books returns a 200 application/json response whose body is an object with a required books array containing book objects with required id, isbn, title, author, status, addedAt, and finishedAt fields.
milestones.note: After adding a book, the user lists the shelf.

milestones.claimTitle: GET /books lists the books on the shelf most recently added first.
milestones.note: The list view should present shelf contents in the documented order.

milestones.claimTitle: Each book object returned by GET /books has integer id, string isbn, string title, string author, status equal to unread or finished, date-time string addedAt, and nullable date-time string finishedAt.
milestones.note: The listed book objects have the documented field types and values.

milestones.claimTitle: GET /books/{id} returns 200 with an application/json book object containing required id, isbn, title, author, status, addedAt, and finishedAt fields.
milestones.note: The user can open the added book by its id.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books/{id}/finish marks the identified book as finished and returns HTTP 200 with the book, now finished, as an application/json object containing the required fields id, isbn, title, author, status, addedAt, and finishedAt.
milestones.note: The path ends with the identified book marked finished.

flows.title: Check service health
flows.goal: A user can confirm the bookclub service is healthy.

milestones.claimTitle: GET /healthz returns a 200 application/json response with required fields status set to "ok" and service set to "bookclub".
milestones.note: This is a standalone health check.

flows.title: Reject unusable book details
flows.goal: A member receives an error when trying to add a book without usable isbn, title, or author details.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books responds with 400 and a JSON object containing an error string when the isbn, title, or author is missing or unusable.
milestones.note: This is a validation error for adding a book.

flows.title: Reject unauthenticated member changes
flows.goal: Requests that require a valid member token return authorization errors when no valid member token is sent.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books responds with 401 and a JSON object containing an error string when no valid member token is sent.
milestones.note: Adding a book is rejected without a valid member token.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books/{id}/finish returns HTTP 401 with an application/json object containing a required error string when no valid member token is sent.
milestones.note: Finishing a book is also rejected without a valid member token.

flows.title: Reject a duplicate book on the shelf
flows.goal: After a book is on the shelf, adding another book with that ISBN returns a duplicate error.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books with a valid member token and an application/json body containing isbn, title, and author responds with 201 and a JSON representation of the book that was added.
milestones.note: The duplicate condition starts with a book already on the shelf.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books responds with 409 and a JSON object containing an error string when a book with that ISBN is already on the shelf.
milestones.note: Adding the same ISBN again returns the documented conflict.

flows.title: Report a missing book lookup
flows.goal: A user receives a not-found error when requesting a book id that does not exist.

milestones.claimTitle: GET /books/{id} returns 404 with an application/json object containing a required string error field when no book has that id.
milestones.note: This is a lookup error for an unknown id.

flows.title: Report an archived book lookup
flows.goal: A user receives an unavailable error when requesting a book that has been archived.

milestones.claimTitle: GET /books/{id} returns 410 with an application/json object containing a required string error field when the book has been archived.
milestones.note: This is a lookup error for an archived book.

flows.title: Reject finishing a missing book
flows.goal: A member receives a not-found error when trying to finish a book id that does not exist.

milestones.claimTitle: POST /books/{id}/finish returns HTTP 404 with an application/json object containing a required error string when no book has the supplied id.
milestones.note: This is a finish request for an unknown id.

flows.title: Start bookclub and manage a first book
flows.goal: A user starts the service, verifies it is healthy, then adds, views, retrieves, and finishes a book through the API.

milestones.claimTitle: Each configuration setting has the documented default value and is overridden by its corresponding environment variable.
On startup, the service applies every migration in `migrations/` against the configured database before it starts listening.
Once the service is up, it prints one line naming the address it is listening on and the database it is using, with the database password masked.
When the service is listening, `GET /healthz` responds with status `200` and body `{"status":"ok","service":"bookclub"}`.
POST /books with a valid member token and an application/json body containing isbn, title, and author responds with 201 and a JSON representation of the book that was added.

GET /books returns a 200 application/json response whose body is an object with a required books array containing book objects with required id, isbn, title, author, status, addedAt, and finishedAt fields.
GET /books/{id} returns 200 with an application/json book object containing required id, isbn, title, author, status, addedAt, and finishedAt fields.

POST /books/{id}/finish marks the identified book as finished and returns HTTP 200 with the book, now finished, as an application/json object containing the required fields id, isbn, title, author, status, addedAt, and finishedAt.
